title: Sensory Accommodations
description: Supports for sensory regulation, including movement breaks and awareness of environmental sensory inputs. Use when the student is sensitive to smells, sounds, or lighting, needs scheduled movement, or shows signs of sensory overload.

source.name: ADayInOurShoes — Ultimate List of IEP Accommodations, Modifications & Strategies (SDIs)

accommodations.text: Give sensory breaks — have the child carry attendance sheets or a few envelopes to the office to allow for movement.
Awareness of sensory issues — smells, sounds, lighting — and adjust as appropriate.
